transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I've called this meeting because we have one mobile bariatric lift available for immediate assignment, and both the North and South inpatient units have patients whose transfer plans are being reviewed for use of the lift. Before I can finalize the assignment, hospital policy requires us to hold a brief equipment-readiness check with physical therapy, facilities, nursing education, and infection prevention. I'd like to go around and hear from each of you so we can assess readiness and determine the best course of action. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to share my physical therapy assessment findings. The South unit patient failed the sit-to-stand assessment and requires a full-body bariatric lift for every bed-to-chair transfer. The North unit patient can currently complete a two-person stand-pivot transfer with a gait belt. Based on these clinical findings, the South unit patient has a more urgent need for the bariatric lift.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important facilities finding. The available lift is the Titan-MB model, which has a 48-inch turning radius. This fits South room 412's 50-inch doorway, but North room 318 has only a 36-inch doorway and cannot safely accommodate this lift. Based on this, the charger must be placed in the South 4B equipment alcove. This aligns with Dr. Chen's clinical assessment that the South unit patient has the more urgent need.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From a nursing education standpoint, I can confirm that three South-unit nurses have completed the lift competency validation. Hospital policy requires two validated staff members for every lift transfer, and South's available coverage with validated staff is 07:00-19:00 daily. This means South can support safe lift operations during those hours, but transfers outside that window would require additional staffing considerations.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: From an infection prevention standpoint, I need to flag an important requirement. The South unit patient is on contact precautions, which means the lift plan requires a dedicated extra-large sling labeled specifically for South room 412, and a documented disinfecting wipe-down of the lift must be performed after each transfer. This is critical to prevent cross-contamination and must be built into the operational plan before the assignment is finalized.
transcript.speaker: A5

decisions.sling_specification: Dedicated extra-large sling labeled specifically for South room 412

commitments.detail: Two validated staff members must be present for every lift transfer, with coverage maintained during the 07:00-19:00 window.
A documented disinfecting wipe-down of the lift must be performed after each transfer to prevent cross-contamination.
The dedicated extra-large sling labeled for South room 412 must remain with the patient and not be shared with other units.
If transfers are needed outside the 07:00-19:00 staffing window, additional staffing considerations must be addressed before proceeding.
